name: Drush Lock
description: Drush commands for acquiring/releasing named locks to protect concurrently executed scripts.
project_description: Drush commands for handling locks. Allows protecting scripts from harmful concurrent execution. Drush is often included in shell scripts that interact with a Drupal installation, and sometimes the same script can run multiple times at roughly the same time when that is undesirable. The motivating use case is starting multiple replicas of a Drupal container on Kubernetes, where each replica automatically applies updates and imports configuration on startup. The commands let a script wait for a named 'lock' before entering a critical section and release it afterwards, so only one process at a time proceeds. These locks are cross-process 'pseudo locks' persisted in the key-value store and do not correspond 1:1 to Drupal's own Locking API (which is per-PHP-process). Note: this is a not-security-advisory-covered, pre-release beta (2.0.0-beta2). Requires only Drush and Drupal core; there is nothing to configure. Provides two commands: lock:wait and lock:release. Current maintainer: Eelke Blok (eelkeblok); developed with funding from Nuffic.
